chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about preparing for the Ihram, so he said: 'In Masjid al-Shajara, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prayed in it, and you will see people entering Ihram from it, so do not do so, until you reach al-Bayda' where the Mi'il, then you enter Ihram as you are in your mounts, saying: 'Here I am, O Allah, here I am, here I am, no partner is there for You, here I am, indeed the praise and the grace is for You and the dominion, no partner is there for You, here I am, with a convenience, with an Umrah until the Hajj.'

key_terms.اَلتَّهَيُّؤُ لِلْإِحْرَامِ: Preparing for the state of Ihram
key_terms.اَلْمِيلُ: Mi'il, a specific landmark or distance marker
key_terms.بِمُتْعَةٍ: With a convenience (referring to the type of Hajj)
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: Talbiyah, the declaration of readiness to serve God
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ اَلشَّجَرَةِ: Masjid al-Shajara, a specific location near Mecca

ai.seo_question: Where is the recommended place to enter Ihram for Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the historical significance of Masjid al-Shajara and the prescribed Miqat at al-Bayda', emphasizing that Ihram should be entered while still on one's mount to maintain ritual purity and continuity. It provides the specific Talbiyah formula for Umrah al-Mut'ah (Umrah linked with Hajj), reflecting the Shia emphasis on the unity of the two pilgrimages as practiced by the Imams. This guidance underscores the scholarly preference for adhering to the specific locations and manners of Ihram as transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt.
